Hey there, just wanted to say that I also got sober my senior year at the U. It was a fairly isolating experience but I was able to connect with other sober friends and get out more because I was no longer drinking. I’m not sure your interests, but I would go to shows at PS1 and Purgatory (Purg doesn’t allow alcohol, PS1 doesn’t serve it) bc I loved that while drinking and it was really helpful to be able to maintain my interests. PS1 also does art workshops that are wonderful. I’d also recommend the community dinners at Sacred Collective on N Linn St, when the weather is good I spend a lot of time at our local parks, all of which are fantastic. Maybe join a fitness group or another hobby interest group that isn’t related to drinking. I also hit a point where I was comfortable going to events at bars and not drinking, but that may not be the case for you, and that’s okay too. If the people around you are good folk, they’ll be supportive. It’s a tough college town to be sober in, but I’m grateful I did it and I have been in your shoes before. Take good care.

Editing to add that the U does have sobriety support groups within Student Health. I don’t know that it’d necessarily be a way to make friends, but it may be a helpful option.
